answer:
FINAL HYPOTHESIS (data-grounded): Summed social capital — the direct sum of the three standardized Z-components, Copper&Gold (ZCU_AU), Amber (Zamber) and Monument Count (ZMonument), per the study-context definition — peaks in the 14th century BCE (BCE 1400–1301; CE −1400…−1301), within the 2nd millennium BCE / Old Bronze Age. The summed Z reaches its maximum of ≈4.24 at the BCE anchors 1400 and 1300 (tied at the century level); resolving this tie with century-bin means of the interpolated yearly sum unambiguously places the peak in the 14th century BCE (mean 4.24), ahead of the 13th century BCE (3.93) and the 12th century BCE (3.62), and the sum stays above 4.0 across BCE 1405–1262. At the per-component level, the increase toward this peak is driven by (a) Copper & Gold, which rises from an early baseline of ≈ −0.34 (before BCE 3300) to a maximum Z = 2.85 in the 13th–12th century BCE (BCE 1200–1100), with a significant positive full-span slope (+0.039 Z/century, p = 0.004) and strong positive rank correlation (Spearman ρ = +0.61, p < 0.0001); and (b) Monument Count, which increases in the later half of the sequence, climbing to a second high of Z = 1.71 at the peak centuries BCE 1400–1300 (1.35 at BCE 1200–1100) with the late-window mean (+0.13) well above the early baseline (−0.69) and positive rank correlation (ρ = +0.43, p = 0.007) — even though monument count's global maximum (Z = 3.95) is an earlier Single-Grave peak at BCE 2700. By contrast (c) Amber does NOT increase: it peaks early (Z = 1.54 in the 4th millennium BCE, BCE 3300–3000) and steadily declines to negative values (slope −0.048 Z/century, p = 0.0003; ρ = −0.43, p = 0.007). In short: summed social capital peaks in the 14th century BCE (2nd millennium BCE); the components that increase are Copper & Gold (toward the 13th–12th century BCE) and Monument Count (in the later, 2nd-millennium phase, especially at BCE 1400–1300), while Amber declines and does not contribute to the late peak.

METHODS/AGGREGATE vs PER-COMPONENT: (1) Aggregate: century-level capital.csv (BCE axis, primary), summed Z = ZCU_AU + Zamber + ZMonument (max 4.238 at BCE 1400 & 1300); century bin resolved via the interpolated yearly sum's century means (CE-bin −1400 mean 4.238 > −1300: 3.933 > −1200: 3.622) → 14th century BCE; CE-equivalent annotation CE −1400…−1301. (2) Per-component: peak value+century, full-span OLS slope and Spearman ρ, and an explicit increase criterion (positive slope AND positive ρ AND late-window mean > early-window mean), plus peak-in-later-half and strong-late-rise checks; results clearly separated from the aggregate. Coverage note: capital.csv spans BCE 4300–500 while the yearly cross-check starts at BCE 4100 (BCE 4300/4200 excluded from yearly, but baseline-identical and peak-neutral); interpolated yearly values exactly equal capital.csv at all 37 overlapping anchors (max abs diff 0.0). Pollen openness (Belau/Woserin) was kept documentation-only and not summed into social capital.

payload.workflow: 1) Parsed capital.csv (BCE axis, comma-decimal handling) and time_series_data.csv (yearly CE axis). 2) Aggregate: summed Z = ZCU_AU + Zamber + ZMonument per century; located max (4.238 @ BCE 1400 & 1300); resolved the tie via century-bin means of the interpolated yearly sum (CopperGold_inter + Amber_inter + MonumentCount_inter) -> 14th century BCE (CE -1400..-1301). 3) Per-component: for each component computed peak value & century (capital + interpolated), full-span OLS slope and Spearman rho over time, early-window (BCE>=3300) vs late-window (BCE<=2000) means, and applied an explicit increase criterion (slope>0 & rho>0 & late_mean>early_mean) plus peak-in-later-half and strong-late-rise checks. 4) Cross-checked interpolated vs capital values at 37 overlapping anchors (max diff 0.0); documented the BCE 4300/4200 coverage gap; kept pollen (Belau/Woserin) documentation-only. 5) Assembled the natural-language hypothesis separating aggregate vs per-component results.
payload.hypothesis: Summed social capital (ZCU_AU + Zamber + ZMonument) peaked in the 14th century BCE (BCE 1400-1301; CE -1400..-1301), within the 2nd millennium BCE / Old Bronze Age (summed Z = 4.24). The components that increase toward/at that peak are Copper & Gold (Z = 2.85 max at BCE 1200-1100; positive significant slope +0.039/century and Spearman rho +0.61) and Monument Count in its later phase (second peak Z = 1.71 at BCE 1400-1300, late mean 0.13 > early mean -0.69, rho +0.43), whereas Amber does not increase (early peak Z = 1.54 in the 4th millennium BCE, then steady decline, slope -0.048/century, rho -0.43).
